correctness.rationale: All quantifiers k>=2, m,n>=0 distinct and normalized Bergman basis are explicit. The monomial multiplier M_z^r differs compactly from isometric S^r because sqrt((j+1)/(j+2))->1. The two slant compositions pick one congruence class modulo k^2 and each maps it bijectively to a cofinite output tail. They share that input class exactly if k^2 divides m-n. In the disjoint case DD*=2I modulo finite rank, while ker(D) has infinite dimension, giving absolute essential spectrum {0,sqrt(2)}. In the shared case the output maps differ by nonzero integer Δ=(k-1)(m-n)/k^2 and the Calkin nonzero corner is I-u^|Δ| for a unitary u with full unit-circle spectrum, giving [0,2]. Equality of Calkin classes transfers the result to Bergman slant operators. Script check_slant.py verified 975014 exact finite identities, not used to infer infinite spectrum.

value.rationale: The exact essential singular spectrum is a natural quantitative invariant left open by qualitative commutativity. It has a sharp arithmetic phase: disjoint residue supports produce the two-point set {0,sqrt(2)}, while identical residues produce an interval [0,2]. The family covers all orders k>=2 and all distinct monomial degrees, and the modulus k² is structurally forced by composition of two k-slant decimations. The classification has value as a complete model for more general slant-symbol essential norms, rather than an arbitrary finite slice or known table computation.
